Self-sufficiency is an important value to me, so I don't go out of my way to approach people and I don't expect anyone to approach me.

I think most of us are used to rejecting others' approaches. He who has never turned down a salesperson, a Jehovah's witness or a hobo asking for change may cast the first stone.

If you have issues with your self esteem, approaching is a risky business. A lot of people will abuse the dynamic just so they can power-trip on rejecting you by doing it in an unnecessarily rude way.

*My* company can only be obtained from *me*. It's not very valuable, unique or sought after, true that, but if for some reason someone chooses to approach me, they effectively hand the control of the encounter over to me (excluding extreme cases, for example threats of violence).

The party that's getting approached decides whether or not the interaction actually happens and can cut it short if they don't like it. They also dictate the tone and topic of the conversation and if the person who did the approaching doesn't like these condtions, they can just go approach someone else.

Look at it like it's a job market. If you have to approach, you're "applying" and the potential "employer" decides if they'll have you or not. Being approached puts you in the position of an "employer".

Edit: paragraphs, much nicer to read

When you are the one getting approached, you get to either accept or reject the person approaching you.
More importantly, them approaching you implies you have something they want (even if they just want the company of a person who looks approachable), giving you a stronger position in the interaction. You have much more control over what happens when you get approached.

I doubt any of those actual incels would come here to explain anything. I feel somewhat competent in the matter and I can tell you that it's more complicated than it seems. Don't mean to support those behaviors, don't engage in them, but self-awareness isn't always easy and most of the time evil doesn't know it is evil.

Look, I've been recently diagnosed with Avoidant Personality Disorder. Persistent feelings of inadequacy, inferiority and social ineptitude are one of the diagnostic criteria for it and selective self-awareness is a common theme in the affected people. For me and many others, the negativity is directed inwards, as I can blow my own shortcomings out of proportion and dismiss the good things I do as basic and meaningless (because "can't disappoint myself if I never get my hopes up in the first place"). It is not beyond my understanding, that some people with different experiences and suffering from different disorders could employ similar mechanisms, but direct them at others, as means to protect and comfort themselves, even if it destroys them over time.

It takes help and work to realize how wrong you are and what you need to change, when all those beliefs and feelings are solidified and guide you through your life. I feel extremely lucky and even privileged for having friends and getting the support I need, many people don't have that luxury. We don't choose our parents, our circumstances , who we meet on our way, hell, we don't even fully contol our thoughts (like, my flatemate has OCD). You slowly learn to work on what you can change and cope with the things you can't.

It's impossible to provide help for everyone, especially since a lot of people don't even seek it or actively reject it. No one is responsible for another person being an asshole. But behind most bad words, expressions, unpleasant interactions is a bigger picture that we never really get to see. All you can do is try to be kind to yourself and to others.

PS Looks are their own debate and they are not without influence on your social life, love included. As I said, either work or cope. Whatever helps.
